current: Ở phần lớn Tây Ban Nha, c trước e, i và z đọc như «th» tiếng Anh; khoá học dùng cách đọc Mỹ Latinh.
proposed: Ở phần lớn Tây Ban Nha, c trước e, i và z đọc như «th» tiếng Anh (zumo, cena); giọng đọc của khoá học là giọng Tây Ban Nha nên bạn sẽ nghe âm này. Đọc như «s» (kiểu Mỹ Latinh) cũng được chấp nhận.
reason: False statement: VARIETY.md makes Peninsular the model and the Kokoro ef_dora/em_alex voices are Castilian (distinción), so telling learners the course uses Latin-American pronunciation contradicts what they hear.

current: Ở Mỹ Latinh, ll và y đọc giống nhau, c trước e, i và z đọc như s.
proposed: Ở hầu hết các vùng nói tiếng Tây Ban Nha, kể cả Tây Ban Nha, ll và y đọc giống nhau (calle, yo). Ở Mỹ Latinh, c trước e, i và z đọc như s.
reason: Yeísmo (ll = y) is the norm in most of Spain too, as the unit-f guidebook itself says; limiting it to Latin America is misleading.

current: Nhóm -er và -ir giống nhau ở hầu hết các ngôi, chỉ khác ở «chúng tôi»: comemos, vivimos.
proposed: Nhóm -er và -ir giống nhau ở hầu hết các ngôi, chỉ khác ở «chúng tôi» và «các bạn» (vosotros): comemos / vivimos, coméis / vivís.
reason: Inaccurate: -er and -ir also differ in the vosotros form (coméis/vivís), which the shortRule of this same card teaches.

current: Khi không phải câu hỏi, các từ này mất dấu: donde vivo (nơi tôi sống).
proposed: Khi không mang nghĩa hỏi, các từ này không có dấu: la ciudad donde vivo (thành phố nơi tôi sống). Câu hỏi gián tiếp vẫn giữ dấu: Pregúntame dónde vivo.
reason: Misleading: indirect questions keep the accent, and the course itself models "pregúntame dónde vivo"; the rule is about relative vs interrogative use, not about the sentence being a question.

current: estar cho điều tạm thời hoặc chỗ ở (Estoy cansado
proposed: estar cho trạng thái tạm thời hoặc vị trí (Estoy cansado
reason: "chỗ ở" means place of residence/accommodation in Vietnamese, which would push learners towards *Estoy en Hanói* for "I live in Hanoi"; the intended meaning is location ("vị trí").

current: Không phải từ nào cũng có cầu nối: work là el trabajo, không phải «la obra» trong mọi ngữ cảnh.
proposed: Vài từ đuôi -ión lại là giống đực: el avión (máy bay), el camión (xe tải).
reason: The current exception is unrelated to the -ción/-dad bridge (work has no -tion/-ty) and confusing; the useful exception is the masculine -ión nouns.

current: tú: bạn bè, người nhỏ tuổi; usted: người lạ, người lớn tuổi, khách hàng.
proposed: tú: bạn bè, người quen, người cùng trang lứa hoặc nhỏ tuổi; usted: người lạ lớn tuổi, người lớn tuổi, khách hàng.
reason: In Spain tú is the default among peers and colleagues, even with strangers of similar age; the card makes it sound restricted to friends and children.

current: Tôi có hai anh em.
proposed: Tôi có hai anh chị em.
reason: "Tôi có hai anh em" reads as "we are two brothers"/"I have brothers"; hermanos is the generic plural for siblings.

current: Muốn xem thực đơn, hãy hỏi *¿El menú, por favor?*
proposed: Muốn xem thực đơn, hãy hỏi *¿La carta, por favor?* (ở Tây Ban Nha, *el menú* thường là suất ăn cố định — *menú del día*).
reason: In Spain one asks for "la carta"; "el menú" means the set menu (the course's own exam text contrasts "menú del día" with "a la carta").

current: *Tengo un hermano.* — Tôi có một anh trai.
proposed: *Tengo un hermano.* — Tôi có một anh trai (hoặc em trai).
reason: The same card explains that hermano covers both older and younger brother; translating only "anh trai" contradicts it.

current: *buenos días* — chào buổi sáng (đến khoảng trưa)
proposed: *buenos días* — chào buổi sáng (ở Tây Ban Nha dùng đến giờ ăn trưa, khoảng 1–2 giờ chiều)
reason: In Spain buenos días runs until lunchtime (around 14:00), later than Vietnamese "trưa".

current: *¿Puede repetir, por favor?* — Ông nhắc lại được không?
proposed: *¿Puede repetir, por favor?* — Ông/bà (anh/chị) nhắc lại giúp được không ạ?
reason: usted is not gendered or age-bound; "Ông" alone is too narrow and lacks the polite particle a Vietnamese speaker would use.

current: Lleva una tortilla, por favor.
proposed: Trae una tortilla, por favor.
reason: The host is asking a guest to bring something to the host's own home, so Peninsular Spanish uses traer (as in dele_a_r1_correo: "trae tu guitarra").

current: El domingo por la mañana tomo el tren para la playa.
proposed: El domingo por la mañana tomamos el tren para la playa.
reason: Singular "tomo" clashes with the following "¿Vienes con nosotros?", which implies a group.

current: el sábado comemos en el restaurante a las siete de la tarde.
proposed: el sábado cenamos en el restaurante a las siete de la tarde.
reason: In Spain comer is the midday meal; an evening meal is cenar (lexemeRef es:w:comer -> es:w:cenar; a Spaniard would expect nine rather than seven, but seven keeps the checkpoint key valid).

current: Por la noche come en un restaurante.
proposed: Por la noche cena en un restaurante.
reason: Evening meal is cenar in Spain; "por la noche come" sounds non-native (update lexemeRefs if comer is listed).

current: Por la noche come en un restaurante con una amiga.
proposed: Por la noche cena en un restaurante con una amiga.
reason: Evening meal is cenar in Spain; "por la noche come" sounds non-native.

current: Mañana por la noche comemos en el restaurante cerca de la estación.
proposed: Mañana por la noche cenamos en el restaurante de al lado de la estación.
reason: Evening meal is cenar; "el restaurante cerca de la estación" without a relative is also stilted.

current: Abierto de martes a sábado, de nueve a seis de la tarde.
proposed: Abierta de martes a sábado, de nueve a seis de la tarde.
reason: The sign is headed "Biblioteca de la ciudad" (feminine) and the course drills agreement (la tienda está abierta); invariable "Abierto" on signs exists but models inconsistent agreement here.

current: Cerrado el domingo y el lunes.
proposed: Cerrada el domingo y el lunes.
reason: Agreement with "Biblioteca" (feminine), same issue as the line above.

current: Abierto de lunes a sábado, de siete a una de la tarde.
proposed: Abierta de lunes a sábado, de siete a una de la tarde.
reason: Heading is "Panadería La Mañana" (feminine); model agreement consistently with what the course teaches.

current: Claro, señora. La mesa cerca de la entrada.
proposed: Claro, señora. Hay una mesa libre cerca de la entrada.
reason: A verbless "La mesa cerca de la entrada" is not how a waiter answers; it needs a verb.

current: La mesa cerca de la puerta es para la señora Martín.
proposed: La mesa de al lado de la puerta es para la señora Martín.
reason: Noun + "cerca de" with no relative is stilted; "la mesa de al lado de la puerta" or "la mesa que está cerca de la puerta" is natural.

current: Entrada de la tienda — a la izquierda, después de la puerta.
proposed: Entrada de la tienda — a la izquierda, después de la escalera.
reason: An entrance "after the door" is illogical; use another landmark.

current: el trabajo es interesante, aunque a veces tengo mucho trabajo.
proposed: el trabajo es interesante, aunque a veces estoy muy ocupado.
reason: Repetition of "trabajo" in one clause reads as non-native in an exam text.

current: H. Hostal Estación: habitaciones baratas cerca del tren.
proposed: H. Hostal Estación: habitaciones baratas al lado de la estación de tren.
reason: "cerca del tren" is unnatural; one is near the station, not near the train.

current: Hoy el supermercado vende la fruta más barata.
proposed: Hoy en el supermercado la fruta está más barata.
reason: As written it means "sells the cheapest fruit"; the intended announcement is that fruit is on offer today.

current: Llueve mucho, lleva paraguas.
proposed: Llueve mucho, coge el paraguas.
reason: The article-less "lleva paraguas" sounds clipped; "coge/llévate el paraguas" is the natural Peninsular advice.

current: Perdone, ¿qué desea tomar?
proposed: Hola, buenos días, ¿qué desea tomar?
reason: "Perdone" is what a customer says to get attention; a waiter taking an order opens with a greeting.

current: Claro, la mesa cerca de la puerta.
proposed: Claro, hay una mesa libre cerca de la puerta.
reason: Verbless reply is stilted for a waiter.

current: Hay siete días en una semana.
proposed: La semana tiene siete días.
reason: English calque (there are seven days in a week); natives say "la semana tiene siete días".

current: ¡Mucho gusto, Nadia! ¿Está bien?
proposed: ¡Mucho gusto, Nadia! ¿Qué tal está?
reason: "¿Está bien?" means "Are you all right?" (as after an accident), not a how-are-you greeting; also update the mirrored transcript in listening.json.

current: ¡Yo también hablo inglés! Bueno, ya sabe todo de mí… o casi.
proposed: ¡Yo también hablo inglés! Bueno, ya sé mucho de usted… ¡Ahora pregúnteme usted a mí!
reason: Logic is reversed: Pablo has been asking about Nadia, so he now knows about her, and the next step is for her to ask him (mirror in listening.json).

current: No pasa nada. Bueno, ya sabe todo de mí… o casi.
proposed: No pasa nada. Bueno, ya sé mucho de usted… ¡Ahora pregúnteme usted a mí!
reason: Same reversed logic as the yes branch.

current: Muy bien. Son dos euros. ¡Gracias, buen día!
proposed: Muy bien. Son dos euros. ¡Gracias, que tenga un buen día!
reason: "¡Buen día!" as a farewell/greeting is Latin-American; Peninsular staff say "¡Que tenga un buen día!" (also fix "¡Y una botella de agua! Son tres euros. ¡Gracias, buen día!").

current: ¡Gracias a usted! ¡Buen día!
proposed: ¡Gracias a usted! ¡Que tenga un buen día!
reason: "¡Buen día!" is Latin-American usage; the course models Peninsular (cf. cafe_bebida: "¡Que tenga un buen día!").

current: ¡De nada! ¡Buen día!
proposed: ¡De nada! ¡Que vaya bien!
reason: "¡Buen día!" is Latin-American; Peninsular "¡Que vaya bien!" or "¡Que tenga un buen día!".

current: ¡Bienvenida! ¿Quieres tomar algo?
proposed: ¡Hola, pasa, pasa! ¿Quieres tomar algo?
reason: The scenario gives the learner no female role, so "Bienvenida" mis-genders male learners; "pasa, pasa" is the natural, neutral welcome.

current: Trả lời lời mời của bạn bạn và nói bạn muốn gì.
proposed: Trả lời lời mời của người bạn và nói bạn muốn uống gì.
reason: "của bạn bạn" is a clumsy calque of "your friend's" and reads like a typo.

current: Hãy nói cảm ơn rất nhiều.
proposed: Hãy nói «cảm ơn nhiều».
reason: Translationese of "say thank you very much"; quoting the phrase is the natural Vietnamese instruction.

current: ¿Quieres venir a cenar a mi casa el sábado a las seis de la tarde?
proposed: ¿Quieres venir a cenar a mi casa el sábado a las nueve?
reason: Dinner at six in the afternoon is culturally wrong for Spain; the prompt does not fix a time.

current: Hola, Lucía: el restaurante es el sábado.
proposed: Hola, Lucía: vamos al restaurante el sábado.
reason: "El restaurante es el sábado" treats the restaurant as an event; natives write "vamos al restaurante el sábado" or "la cena es el sábado".

current: Hola, Ana: el café es a las dos.
proposed: Hola, Ana: tomamos un café a las dos.
reason: Ambiguous and slightly odd ("the café is at two"); a natural note says "tomamos un café a las dos" (same for cp5_note_ana).

current: Leo vive en Madrid y trabaja.
proposed: Leo vive y trabaja en Madrid.
reason: "... y trabaja" dangling at the end sounds unfinished.

current: Es por la noche
proposed: Es de noche
reason: Describing the time of day shown in a picture, Spanish uses "Es de noche"; "Es por la noche" answers "when is it?".

current: Hay siete días en una semana
proposed: La semana tiene siete días
reason: English calque; natives say "La semana tiene siete días".

current: Mamá, ¿dónde está Toby?
proposed: Papá, ¿dónde está Toby?
reason: The answer comes from the father (male voice B, translated "Bố", and "Ana y su padre van por el pueblo"), so Ana must address "Papá".

current: No sé, hija. Vamos a buscar.
proposed: No sé, hija. Vamos a buscarlo.
reason: buscar needs its object here; "Vamos a buscar" sounds incomplete.

current: Un día, Toby no está en la casa.
proposed: Un día, Toby no está en casa.
reason: One's own home is "en casa" without article; the article models a typical learner error.

current: Ana, su padre y Toby vuelven a la casa por el puente.
proposed: Ana, su padre y Toby vuelven a casa por el puente.
reason: "volver a casa" (own home) takes no article.

current: En la casa, la madre de Ana prepara una sopa.
proposed: En casa, la madre de Ana prepara una sopa.
reason: "En casa" for one's own home.

current: Toby, ¡no vas sin mí!
proposed: Toby, ¡no te vayas sin mí!
reason: "no vas sin mí" is not idiomatic as a reproach; the fixed chunk is "¡no te vayas sin mí!" (or colloquial "¡tú no te vas sin mí!").

current: Hola, mis niños. ¿Tienen hambre?
proposed: Hola, mis niños. ¿Tenéis hambre?
reason: A Spanish grandmother addresses her grandchildren with vosotros; ustedes here is Latin-American and breaks the Peninsular model.

current: ¿Quieren sopa?
proposed: ¿Queréis sopa?
reason: Same vosotros issue with the grandchildren.

current: Pablo muốn thêm một đĩa súp nữa.
proposed: Pablo muốn ăn thêm một bát súp nữa.
reason: Vietnamese serves soup in a "bát", not a "đĩa"; "plato de sopa" is a bowl/serving of soup.

current: Dos días pasan.
proposed: Pasan dos días.
reason: Unmarked word order with pasar is verb-first (cf. "Pasan dos semanas" in la_rodilla_de_javier).

current: Hôm nào mình cũng sẽ đến tiệm bánh đó.
proposed: Hôm nào đó mình cũng sẽ đến tiệm bánh ấy.
reason: "Hôm nào ... cũng" means "every day", the opposite of "Un día voy a ir" ("some day I will go").

current: No sé. Creo que el museo no está en este camino.
proposed: No sé. Creo que este no es el camino del museo.
reason: "el museo no está en este camino" is a calque; natives say "este no es el camino" / "vamos mal".

current: Tienen que caminar recto.
proposed: Tienen que ir todo recto.
reason: "caminar recto" means walk upright; directions use "(ir/seguir) todo recto", as the course teaches in unit-u.

current: Clara y Jorge caminan recto y llegan a la plaza.
proposed: Clara y Jorge van todo recto y llegan a la plaza.
reason: Same "caminar recto" issue.

current: La canción pasa, y la casa está en silencio.
proposed: La canción termina y la casa está en silencio.
reason: A song does not "pasar"; it ends ("termina").

current: Cuando yo era un niño, mi padre tenía este barco.
proposed: Cuando yo era niño, mi padre tenía este barco.
reason: "Cuando era niño" takes no article; "era un niño" is an English calque.

current: No, Rosa. Soy un abuelo.
proposed: No, Rosa. Ya soy mayor.
reason: "Soy un abuelo" does not convey "I'm too old now" (the Vietnamese "Ông già rồi"); natives say "Ya soy mayor".

current: Llegan a la casa cuando la nube llega al pueblo.
proposed: Llegan a casa cuando la nube llega al pueblo.
reason: "llegar a casa" (own home) without article.

current: Después, van a la panadería por un pastel.
proposed: Después, van a la pastelería a comprar una tarta.
reason: In Spain a birthday cake is "una tarta" and "ir por" is Latin-American (Peninsular "ir a por"/"a comprar").

current: Pero cuando abre la ventana, mira la lluvia.
proposed: Pero cuando abre la ventana, ve que llueve.
reason: mirar = look at deliberately; perceiving the rain is ver ("ve que llueve").

current: Tengo frío y la lluvia está en toda mi ropa.
proposed: Tengo frío y tengo toda la ropa mojada.
reason: "la lluvia está en toda mi ropa" is a non-native calque; natives say "tengo la ropa mojada".

current: Cuando salen del cine, ya no hay lluvia.
proposed: Cuando salen del cine, ya no llueve.
reason: Spanish says "ya no llueve", not "ya no hay lluvia".

current: Paula, ¿estoy bien?
proposed: Paula, ¿qué tal estoy?
reason: "¿Estoy bien?" sounds like asking about health; asking how one looks is "¿qué tal estoy?" / "¿cómo me queda?".

current: Javier no ve una caja y golpea la caja con el pie.
proposed: Javier no ve una caja y tropieza con ella.
reason: Repeating "la caja" is clumsy and "golpear con el pie" (kick) is not tripping; natural is "tropieza con ella".

current: Y no puede correr en dos semanas.
proposed: Y no puede correr durante dos semanas.
reason: "en dos semanas" means "in two weeks' time"; duration is "durante dos semanas".

current: ¡Hola! ¿Qué hacen aquí?
proposed: ¡Hola! ¿Qué hacéis aquí?
reason: A brother speaking to his sister and her friend uses vosotros in Spain; ustedes is Latin-American here.

current: Y yo creo que eres un ladrón.
proposed: ¡Y yo creía que eras un ladrón!
reason: Present "creo que eres" says "I believe you are a thief" now; the intended "I thought you were" (Vietnamese "tưởng") needs the imperfect, already used in other stories.

current: Miro una película en internet.
proposed: Veo una película en internet.
reason: One "ve" a film (ver una película, as elsewhere in the course); "miro una película" is non-native.

current: Marcos, ¿y tu tarea?
proposed: Marcos, ¿y los deberes?
reason: Homework is "los deberes" in Spain (used in the DELE B notice); "la tarea" is Latin-American.

current: Mamá, la próxima vez voy a hacer mi tarea.
proposed: Mamá, la próxima vez voy a hacer los deberes.
reason: Peninsular "los deberes".

current: Mañana vamos a ver.
proposed: Mañana lo vemos.
reason: "Mañana vamos a ver" reads as "tomorrow we will watch"; the idiom "we'll see" is "ya lo veremos" / "mañana lo vemos".

current: Marcos tiene quince años y va a la escuela.
proposed: Marcos tiene quince años y va al instituto.
reason: A 15-year-old in Spain goes to "el instituto"; "la escuela" suggests primary school.

current: No es un problema. ¿Quieren algo para beber?
proposed: No pasa nada. ¿Quieren algo de beber?
reason: "No es un problema" is a calque of "no problem"; natives say "No pasa nada", and "algo de beber" is the set phrase.

current: Perdón, señor. Es mi lugar.
proposed: Perdone, señor. Es mi asiento.
reason: A train seat is "asiento"/"sitio" in Spain; "lugar" is Latin-American usage here, and "Perdone" matches her usted.

current: ¡Oh, perdón! Mi lugar es el número once.
proposed: ¡Ay, perdón! Mi asiento es el número once.
reason: Same "lugar" issue; "¡Ay!" is the Spanish interjection ("¡Oh!" is bookish).

current: Treinta años trabajo en este tren.
proposed: Trabajo en este tren desde hace treinta años.
reason: Fronted "Treinta años trabajo" is not idiomatic; duration is "desde hace treinta años" (or "llevo treinta años trabajando").

current: ¡Hola a todos! Soy Miguel, su profesor.
proposed: ¡Hola a todos! Soy Miguel, vuestro profesor.
reason: A dance teacher in Spain addresses the group with vosotros; "su profesor" is Latin-American or overly formal.

current: ¡Sí, por favor!
proposed: ¡Sí, claro!
reason: Answering an invitation "¿vienes...?" with "por favor" is a calque; natives say "¡Sí, claro!".

current: Tres euros.
proposed: La señora dice: «Tres euros el kilo».
reason: Lines 10 and 11 are both speaker A (same ef_dora voice) although the second is the vendor, so listeners cannot hear the turn change; a narrator frame fixes it.
